analysis.investment_thesis: Angel One is a discount broker with no durable competitive moat in a commoditised, regulation-sensitive industry — and the 2026 financials reveal exactly what happens when regulatory headwinds hit: revenue flat, net profit down 22% YoY to ₹915 Cr, and borrowings exploding from ₹788 Cr (2023) to ₹7,951 Cr (2026). This is a business whose best years may already be behind it.
key_strengths: Demonstrated scale: revenue CAGR of 31.4% over 9 years, reaching ₹5,137 Cr — Angel One became a genuine mass-market platform
Strong technology infrastructure via Super App and Smart API, with large registered client base creating some network effect
Forward P/E of 20x is relatively modest, suggesting some of the bad news is now priced in
key_risks: SEBI's F&O regulation changes in 2024 directly decimated the industry's most profitable revenue stream — this regulatory risk is structural, not temporary
Borrowings grew 10x in three years (₹788 Cr → ₹7,951 Cr) while profits fell; the leverage trajectory is deeply concerning
Operating cash flow was -₹4,142 Cr in 2026 and -₹1,860 Cr in 2025 — the business is consuming capital at an alarming rate
red_flags: Net profit peaked at ₹1,172 Cr (2025) and fell 22% to ₹915 Cr (2026) — the earnings trajectory has reversed
Borrowings of ₹7,951 Cr vs equity of ₹6,118 Cr: D/E of 0.76 and rising fast, driven by margin funding book growth while core earnings shrink
Discount broking has zero moat — price competition is brutal, switching costs are nil, and platforms like Zerodha and Groww compete aggressively for the same customers
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I have always been skeptical of financial intermediaries whose economics depend entirely on market activity levels they cannot control. Angel One's results validate that concern: when SEBI tightened F&O rules in 2024, the company's most profitable revenue stream was curtailed, and profits have since declined despite the company deploying enormous capital. Borrowings jumping from ₹788 Cr to ₹7,951 Cr over three years while profits fall is a combination that makes me deeply uncomfortable.

The business also lacks the pricing power I require. A discount broker is, by definition, competing on price — there is nothing proprietary about executing a stock trade. Angel One's impressive growth was largely a function of a bull market in Indian retail participation and F&O volumes, both of which have been constrained by regulation. I see no clear path to re-establishing the 2024-25 earnings peak, and I refuse to pay 32x earnings for a business in earnings decline with rapidly rising debt.
